recent.title: Verity
recent.author: Colleen Hoover
recent.review: verity really had me glued to the page for hours just to finish it and sit there thinking… huh did i even LIKE that ?! because i absolutely ATE this up. like once i finally had enough free time to properly sit down and read , it was over. i was flying through chapters because i needed to know what the hell was going on in this house. the premise is SO good too. lowen gets hired to finish a bestselling author’s series after verity is left unable to write following an accident , moves into her house to go through her notes and then finds an autobiography she was definitely not meant to read. obviously i was seated. and for a while i was genuinely so invested in figuring out what the hell was happening in this house. is verity actually as helpless as everyone thinks she is ? is lowen losing her mind ? who's lying ?? i LOVE that kind of psychological thriller where you are constantly questioning whose version of reality you are supposed to believe in other words peak gaslight 😌 unfortunately , somewhere along the way this stopped feeling like a thriller and started feeling like i had accidentally been forced into third wheeling verity and jeremy’s marriage. WHY WAS THERE SO MUCH SEX. i understand what the book was trying to show us. verity is obsessed with jeremy. she needs his attention constantly and practically measures the success of their entire marriage based on whether that man wants to sleep with her. insaneee behaviour , no doubt , and i understood that VERY quickly. we did not need to keep proving it to me over and over and OVER again in excruciating detail. this book is literally the definition of TMI. and somehow after surviving verity and jeremy , i then had to third wheel lowen and jeremy instead. CAN EVERYONE IN THIS HOUSE PLEASE KEEP THEIR HANDS TO THEMSELVES FOR FIVE MINUTES ! i'm begginggg. also i am breaking my silence : i did not like lowen. girlie walks into a house where a man’s severely injured wife is literally upstairs and within approximately five business days she's already thirsting over her husband ??! jeremy is just as guilty here like he thought he was slick. the manuscript itself was probably the strongest part because manuscript verity may genuinely be a psychopath. some of the things she says about her own children are so borderline crazy and yet somehow the thing that made me most uncomfortable was STILL the way she talked about jeremy and their sex life. that should tell you everything. i know the point is that we are supposed to question whether the manuscript was real or whether the letter was telling the truth , and i actually like that we never get a definitive answer. both versions of verity are interesting to me. BUT THAT WAS THE TWIST in this 'thriller' ? maybe i have simply read too many thrillers because i was waiting for the moment where everything would click into place , instead we got another document (letter this time) going “actually maybe everything you just read was bullshit” and then the book basically ended. OH ALSO , i'm not done with LOW... her suddenly becoming all emotional and conflicted at the end was sending me because girl YOU WANTED THIS MAN. you inserted yourself into this disaster and now suddenly we are standing around contemplating morality ? the entire house is full of people making the worst possible decision at every opportunity and then acting shocked when everything goes to shit. so yeah , i genuinely do not know what happened here. this did not scare me. **the writing scared me.** there are so many better thrillers that create actual tension and psychological horror without making me feel like i need to dip the book in bleach afterwards. yet i cannot even pretend i was bored because i read this ridiculously fast. so congratulations verity. you completely hooked me , grossed me out , pissed me off and then somehow made me question why i spent all that time reading you in the first place. 2 stars ✨ i am STILL watching the movie because apparently i have not suffered enough. i’m way too curious to see how the hell they adapt all of THIS on screen and whether the movie somehow manages to make it work better... but hey anne hathaway and dakota johnson , at least we'll have good acting.

recent.title: (Mostly) Human Resources (Entity Case Files, #1)
recent.author: Grace Viall
recent.review: okay spooky season is still going strong because mostly human resources just completely blindsided me and i LOVEEE when a book does that. i went into this almost completely blind. literally the only thing i knew was that it was fairyloot’s cozy pick and i was sold the SECOND i saw their edition. i saw the teaser reels , saw that dark spooky aesthetic mixed with pink and immediately started hunting it down because apparently that is all it takes to get me. like no regrets too because this edition is genuinely insane. whoever designed this thing deserves everything because HOW do you make something look like it belongs directly in halloween while also making it pink and pretty at the same time ?? i could probably spend the next ten hours yapping about the artwork alone but unfortunately i do actually have to review the book. which brings me to the funniest part because i went into this expecting a cozy mystery. that was hmm certainly an assumption... i have spent YEARS watching true crime documentaries and listening to people online tell stories about demons , unexplained things in the woods and every horrifying “i live near the appalachian mountains and THIS happened to me” story that somehow always finds me on tiktok when i am getting ready , lying in bed or already unable to sleep. so once i realized this book was actually leaning into supernatural creatures and folklore ?? ohhh i was seated and lockedd in. alexis works in HR for an organization responsible for controlling and researching supernatural entities , while nic is the head of their research and cataloging department. when their coworker elliot disappears after following a lead about a nearly extinct creature called a hollow walker , alexis and nic end up pulled into figuring out what happened to him. that is basically all you need to know because this is one of those books that is SO much more fun when you have absolutely no idea what direction it is about to take. i genuinely have to apologize because there were multiple times where something started happening and i thought “surely they are not actually going there. this is supposed to be cozy.” then my suspicions get confirmed in like the next chapter. every single time i tried to underestimate this book because of the cozy label , it basically looked me dead in the face and proved me wrong. and THAT is exactly the kind of genre crossing i want more of because mostly human resources somehow sits right between mystery/thriller , fantasy , and romance without feeling like somebody threw five different books into a blender and hoped for the best. it actually ended up working this time. the mystery constantly gave me something to chase , the supernatural parts were genuinely interesting and the book was completely willing to let some of its darker moments actually be dark. then you have the romance running through everything without it completely swallowing the plot. there is a lot happening here and somehow none of it felt like the book was fighting itself over what genre it wanted to be. was pretty busy while reading this as well and still kept thinking about it whenever i was doing something else because i just wanted to get back to the story. i never really hit that point where i was checking how many pages i had left or waiting for something interesting to finally happen. once i was in , i was IN. my biggest complaint is probably the banter between alexis and nic , and even then i did not hate it. i am literally eighteen years old so who am i to sit here acting like i am above slightly childish banter 😭 but there were definitely moments where something in the back of my head kept reminding me that these are not teenagers. these are grown working adults with JOBS. the book never explicitly tells us their ages so i have mentally placed our mains somewhere twentyish , but sometimes their arguments made me desperately want to pretend otherwise. alexis herself is also lowkey funny by mistake because she spends so much of the book presenting herself as this massive HR rule follower while simultaneously hiding some extremely important information and secretly researching the entity attached to her. GIRL ?? hello ?? HR would like a word with HR. but i actually think the book handles that contradiction really well. alexis knows what she is doing is questionable and you understand why she feels like she cannot exactly walk into work and announce everything that is happening to her. by the end she also has to sit with the possibility that keeping certain things hidden may have helped send everything spiralling in the direction it did. i really liked seeing that guilt actually affect her instead of the story brushing it aside because she is the main character and therefore obviously did nothing wrong. if there is one thing i REALLY wanted more of though , it is the lore. this book has so many supernatural creatures and so much fictional folklore mixed with things that feel rooted in the kinds of stories people have been telling about places like the appalachian mountains forever. because of that , i sometimes wanted the book to actually stop and explain things a little more instead of leaving us to piece together clues and make guesses about how everything works. especially because there are still so many questions around alexis , the entity attached to her and what exactly is happening in this world. and if you know who i mean when i say the person who helped her in the woods... yeah. WHO ARE YOU. WHAT WAS THAT. COME BACK. but i also understand why the book does not give us everything immediately. this is the first book in a trilogy and i would rather finish book one desperately curious about the lore than read 600 pages because the author decided every piece of supernatural history needed its own chapter. there is clearly a shit ton still being set up here and now i am very curious about how much of it is going to come back later. i'm also wishing we got slightly more from the ending because everything is left in this weird limbo where i can genuinely see book two starting off anywhere. there are things about these characters and their circumstances that are still very uncertain , and then the book ended right when i had become properly invested in all of them. mostly human resources was such a fun surprise and another debut that has immediately made me interested in whatever this author does next. it is not a life changing book and there are definitely things i want the series to dig into more , but as the beginning of a trilogy ?? this did exactly what it needed to do. more importantly , i NEED more books to get weird with their genres like this. give me the mystery. give me the horror. throw some fantasy creatures in there. apparently add an enemies to lovers office romance while you are at it. if you are going to mix five different things together , THIS is how you convince me it can actually work. 4.25 stars ✨

recent.title: The Caretaker
recent.author: Marcus Kliewer
recent.review: the caretaker has me in the VERY annoying space of finishing a book in basically one sitting , having a genuinely good time with it and then somehow still not knowing what the hell i want to rate it 😭 spooky season is finally here which means i can pretend i have an excuse to read horror nonstop even though we all know i would be doing that anyway. thankfully , this was such a good way to switch the tone because i absolutely BREEZED through it. i started reading and suddenly the entire day was gone because i needed to know what was happening next. the premise is also sooo good. macy desperately needs money and answers an ad for a housesitting job that pays suspiciously well. all she has to do is stay in this house and follow a set of instructions. sounds easy enough , right ?? well hmm apparently not if your name is macy. i am sorry but this woman was driving me insaneeee and it did not get better too... some of these tasks were genuinely so simple and somehow she kept failing them over and over again. switch off the lights. follow the instructions. maybe , just maybe do not immediately ignore the extremely concerning rules attached to the suspiciously high paying job you found online. CALL ME JEMMA because i was basically her younger sister throughout this entire book. she is quite literally the only person with a functioning survival instinct and you can practically hear her voice inside macy’s head telling her what she SHOULD be doing. get out. lock in. this job is one gigantic red flag. macy hears all of this perfectly well before deciding she knows better anyway. i was fighting for my LIFE. somehow though , that frustration also made this ridiculously readable because every time macy made things worse for herself , i needed to know what was going to happen next. the atmosphere helped too. this was not necessarily scary scary , but the entire book has this gloomy , unsettling feeling hanging over it that worked really well for me. my biggest problem is that we get SO many interesting ideas and literally nothing is explained. i wanted more about the house , the entity , the people reaching out through the phone + whatever exactly is happening with this other already doomed reality lingering around the edges of the story. the book gives you just enough information to understand what is happening on the surface and then basically goes “okay trust me” before moving on. the ending made that even worse for me. i understand what the book is doing with the mental health metaphor and the bleakness definitely feels intentional , but i still wanted more explanation and some idea of what comes after everything that happens. tbh , this is one of those books where i think a sequel could make me like the first book even more. explore the aftermath , show me more of whatever exists on the other side and actually dig into the history behind all of this. if that ever gets announced ?? yeah i will absolutely be there. so this is a VERY conflicted 3.5 for me. i binge read the entire thing , genuinely enjoyed myself and would still recommend it , but between macy testing the absolute limits of my patience and the book leaving way too many of its best questions unanswered , i cannot quite round it up. still VERY interested to see what this author does next though. 3.5 stars ✨ rounded down

recent.title: The Demon Star
recent.author: Jesse Aragon
recent.review: the demon star really looked me dead in the face with one of the coolest horror concepts ever and then somehow made me fight for my life just to finish it , which totally threw me straight off. i went into this with pretty high expectations , especially because my broken binding edition is SO spooky and fits the entire vibe i wanted perfectly. HONESTLY ?? the beginning made me think i was about to love this. demons can literally crawl into people’s ears and possess them , the world outside the main city is basically a wasteland where demons can bleed through and there is this whole conflict between the church , gods and everything they are trying to keep out. jacen being an exorcist who is devoted to the church while carrying around his own trauma and rightly starting to question everything , also gives the story an amazing starting point. the demon star is VERY ambitious , definitely too much for its own good. the world is so complicated that the book constantly has to stop and explain something new to you. after a while it felt like every time the story finally started moving again , i was hit with another wall of information. i almost dnfed this so many times because once i crossed the halfway point i genuinely did not care what happened anymore. the mystery had lost most of its tension and there was nothing else keeping me hooked. and this definitely is not a case of sci-fi simply not being for me because i loved the girl with a thousand faces and project hail mary + dystopian settings have always been my thing. there are genuinely cool ideas in here. i just felt like i was being told so much about this world that i never really got the chance to properly experience it. the relationships did not help either. i knew there was going to be a poly relationship before reading , but the development was so rushed that when it finally became a thing i genuinely felt like i had missed several chapters… one connection gets some backstory , but then another person enters the equation so quickly that i was sitting there like WHEN exactly did we get here ?! even the ending felt weirdly tame after all that buildup. some of these threats literally were built up the entire book then once someone actually confronted them , the resolutions felt surprisingly easy. i kept waiting for everything to finally explode and instead my reaction was basically… oh. that’s it ?? there is absolutely an interesting book somewhere inside the demon star. the premise is fantastic and i can appreciate just how much the author was trying to do with this world , but the execution completely lost me. considering demons were literally crawling into people’s ears , i really should not have been this bored. 1.5 stars rounded up to 2 ✨
